title: zoe-henderson-sre-oncall-scratchpad-2026-03-16
body:
Date: 2026-03-16
On-call: Zoe Henderson (primary)
Backup: Noah Chen
Shift notes: morning -> handoff from Lena at 08:00; no outstanding paging at handoff. Quiet first half, spike around 11:20.

11:18 PAGE: High 95th latency for /v1/generate (prod-us-west-2)
- Signal: elevated p95 (1.2s -> 3.8s), error rate 0.8% (timeout and 502s) from serving-runtime nodes pool-gpu-5.
- Immediate triage: checked SLO dashboards (console -> per-route latency), traced to node set pool-gpu-5 showing KV cache thrashing and OOM warnings in logs.
- Mitigation: scaled pool-gpu-5 +2 nodes using autoscale API (policy: immediate-burst). Also toggled fallback-routing to model-variant small-quant (to reduce memory pressure) for a subset of traffic (10%).
- Result: p95 came down to ~1.5s after 8 minutes, errors dropped to 0.1%.
- Ticket: INC-2026-032 created (linked). Assigned to @lena for follow-up and root cause.

Notes during incident:
- Observed kernel-level retries in logs (nvml/memory reclaim) may be a regression from the runtime change deployed 2026-03-15 (see PR #512).
- Cache eviction TTLs looked shorter than expected: prefix cache hit rate dropped from 82% -> 34%. Possibly misconfiguration in cache size policy for that pool.
- Action taken: increased cache size flag for pool-gpu-5 (runtime config set: cache.max_bytes=180GB -> 240GB) as temporary; need permanent fix.

Post-incident follow-ups (TO DO):
- [ ] Postmortem draft for INC-2026-032 (owner: Zoe, due 2026-03-19). Include timeline, mitigations, and link deployment PR.
- [ ] Revert/adjust runtime patch from 2026-03-15 if reproduces locally (owner: Lena). Test with smaller repro workloads.
- [ ] Add alert to detect sudden cache hit-rate drops (>30% delta within 10m) (owner: Michael). Create ENG ticket and alert rule.
- [ ] Runbook update: add section for \"GPU pool KV cache thrash\" with quick mitigations + autoscale checklist + commands. (owner: Zoe). Confluence page: confluence:runbooks/cache-eviction
- [ ] Schedule follow-up post-incident meeting with serving-runtime team and release-eng (target: 2026-03-18).

Other items during shift:
- 14:05 Minor alarm: RPS spike for embeddings endpoint in eu-west-1 traced to customer demo traffic (customer: acme-corp). Coordinated with CS to ask them to scale load; no customer-impacting errors. Note: consider adding a short-term rate-limit rule for demo accounts. (added to ENG-3421)

Run commands & snippets used (kept here as quick reference):
- Check pool status: curl -sS https://console.internal/api/pools/pool-gpu-5 | jq .status
- Scale pool: curl -X POST https://console.internal/api/pools/pool-gpu-5/scale -d '{"delta":2}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer ****'
- Toggle fallback routing: http POST https://console.internal/api/routing/policies apply:='{"route":"/v1/generate","percent":10,"variant":"small-quant"}'

Observations/questions for handoff:
- Need clear SLA for autoscale single-step burst it recovered, but burst capacity was slow to warm up. Are warm pools healthy? Who owns pre-warm config? (ping platform-eng)
- The runtime change in PR #512 mentions \"buffered eviction improvement\" could be the culprit. Request: reproduction plan + metrics comparison for last 7 days.

Handoff checklist to night oncall:
- INC-2026-032: follow-ups assigned; waiting on Lena for repro & Michael for alert rule.
- Cache config was increased temporarily; note in runbook and in incident ticket.
- Monitor p95 for /v1/generate for next 24h (alert threshold temporarily lowered to 1.2s).
- Contact list: Lena Garcia (primary on-call for serving-runtime), Michael Baker (observability), Noah Chen (backup).

Rough timeline for postmortem (notes to self):
- Collect logs + flamegraphs from pool-gpu-5 (2026-03-15 -> 2026-03-16).
- Compare cache hit rates pre/post-deploy.
- Verify kernel & driver uptimes across nodes in pool.
- Confirm whether deployment PR #512 included configuration change to cache.max_bytes. If so, revert or patch.

Loose ideas / brainstorming (not urgent):
- Consider a \"canary warm pool\" that maintains a small number of pre-warmed nodes to reduce cold-start memory churn for popular models.
- Add synthetic (low-cost) continuous tests that spike cache pressure to detect regressions earlier.

Quick TODO list (personal):
- [ ] Draft postmortem intro & timeline (today before EOD).
- [ ] Create ENG ticket for alert rule and link to incident.
- [ ] Add short note in runbook with commands and escalation matrix.
- [ ] Follow-up meeting invite (30m) with serving-runtime + release-eng.

Random notes / scratch: 
- Customer ACME demo at 14:00 used vectorized batch size 256 flagged as risky for production demo accounts. Add recommendation to docs.
- Remember to sync with release-engineering about canary window length (they recently shortened it to 10 minutes, maybe too short).

End of shift summary (brief): handled p95 spike for /v1/generate caused by cache thrash after 2026-03-15 runtime change. Mitigations applied (scale + fallback + cache bump). Follow-ups assigned. Next: postmortem + alerting + runbook updates.

Signed,
Zoe
